text: FINAL DIAGNOSIS: PART 1: THYROID, TOTAL THYROIDECTOMY (29 GRAMS) -. A. PAPILLARY THYROID CARCINOMA, TWO FOCI (2.3 CM AND 0.4 CM), CONFINED TO THYROID. B. LARGEST FOCUS, LEFT LOBE (2.3 CM), ENCAPSULATED FOLLICULAR VARIANT WITH NO CAPSULAR OR. ANGIOLYMPHATIC INVASION. C. PATHOLOGIC STAGE: pT2NO. D. ISTHMIC FOCUS (0.4 CM), MICROCARCINOMA WITH CYSTIC CHANGE, NO ANGIOLYMPHATIC INVASION. (see comment). E. PATHOLOGIC STAGE: pT1aNO. F. THREE LYMPH NODES (ONE LEFT AND ONE RIGHT PERITHYROIDAL AND ONE ISTHMIC), NO TUMOR. PRESENT (0/3). G. NODULAR THYROID HYPERPLASIA WITH CHRONIC LYMPHOCYTIC THYROIDITIS. PART 2: PARATHYROID, 1/2 LEFT SUPERIOR, EXCISION (153 MG) -. ENLARGED HYPERCELLULAR PARATHYRO(D. PART 3: PARATHYROID, 1/3 LEFT INFERIOR, EXCISION 794 MG) -. SLIGHTLY ENLARGED MILDLY HYPERCELLULAR. PART 4: LYMPH NODES, CENTRAL COMPARTMENT, SELECTIVE DISSECTION -. A. FIVE LYMPH NODES, NO TUMOR PRESENT (0/5). B. THYROID TISSUE WITH CHRONIC LYMPHOCYTIC THYROIDITIS. C. SPECIMEN ENTIRELY SUBMITTED FOR HISTOLOGIC EVALUATION. PART 5: PARATHYROID, 1/4 RIGHT SUPERIOR, EXCISION (18 MG) -. NORMOCELLULAR PARATHYROID TISSUE. COMMENT: PART 1: The carcinoma is subcapsular, but shows no fibrosis. While technically there are two foci, these are different. papiliary carcinoma subtypes, and it can be argued that there is no intragiandular spread with respect to this. microcarcinoma, which is cystic and of conventional histologic subtype.
